newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uzbek gold tender result delayed until end of May.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek gold tender result delayed until end of May.

text.p: Uzbekistan has postponed a tender result for seven gold fields with estimated reserves of 1,720 tonnes of gold until the end of May, a source at the republic's State Geology Committee said on Wednesday.

"The announcement of the result has been delayed as we are waiting for the arrival of a delegation from one Western company which could be the winner of the tender," the source, who declined to be named, told Reuters by telephone from the Uzbek capital Tashkent.
He would not name the company but said it was scheduled to arrive in Tashkent for negotiations on May 20.
Results of the ex-Soviet state's tender, first announced in June last year, have been delayed several times.

The largest gold field in the tender is Dzhetymtauskaya, with reserves estimated by the committee at 400 tonnes. The Karamurunskaya field contains estimated reserves of 250 tonnes of gold and 2.5 million tonnes of copper.
Uzbekistan will demand a minimum 50 percent stake in the projects which will be free of tax for three years.
About 17 companies competed for the fields including Britain's RTZ Corp Plc, Toronto-listed Nelson Gold, Montreal-listed Mazarin Mining Corp and Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd.
